_source: References §4.2, §4.4, §4.6, §4.7, §7.1, §2.4. Examples only; a client's own scope is set in writing at onboarding.

situations.label: A desktop won’t load.
situations.answer: The platform is ours: the session hosts, the standard image, the host pool.

situations.label: It’s patch day.
situations.answer: Operating system and Microsoft 365 app patching run on schedule. Nobody files a ticket.

situations.label: Monday, 9:00. Everyone signs in at once.
situations.answer: Capacity follows demand, as your people sign in.

situations.label: The fix needs Microsoft.
situations.answer: We own the escalation and the communication.

situations.label: The accounting system’s report is wrong.
situations.answer: Application-level support stays with the software’s vendor. We run the infrastructure and operating system it needs.

situations.label: The office internet is down.
situations.answer: That’s your internet provider. You knew that at onboarding, not today.

situations.label: A laptop screen cracked.
situations.answer: Hardware isn’t ours. But the work was never on the laptop: sign in from another device.
